question: How do you structure a large Angular monorepo app?
shortAnswer: Feature folders with routes, shared UI lib, core singleton services, and clear public APIs.
detailedAnswer: Use Nx or workspace libs. Avoid deep cross-feature imports. Lazy load features. Keep domain logic out of dumb components.

question: Smart vs presentational components in Angular?
shortAnswer: Smart containers fetch/orchestrate; presentational receive inputs and emit outputs.
detailedAnswer: Presentational components are easier to test and reuse. Don't put HttpClient in every leaf component.

question: When do you introduce a state library (NgRx, SignalStore) vs services?
shortAnswer: Complex shared workflows, time-travel/debug needs, or many writers → store; simple feature state → signal services.
detailedAnswer: Avoid premature NgRx. Signal-based stores often suffice. Consistency matters more than brand of store.

question: How should API models differ from view models?
shortAnswer: Map DTOs to UI-friendly models in an anti-corruption layer; don't bind raw API shapes everywhere.
detailedAnswer: Protects UI from backend churn. Centralize adapters. Validate at boundaries.

question: Design auth + feature modules for an enterprise Angular app.
shortAnswer: Core auth service, interceptor, guards; features lazy-loaded; shared UI; environment config tokens.
detailedAnswer: Centralize permissions. Prefer canMatch for role routes. Keep secrets off the client.

question: What is the facade pattern in Angular feature design?
shortAnswer: A facade service exposes a narrow API over multiple stores/APIs so components stay simple.
detailedAnswer: Helps hide NgRx complexity. Don't create facades that become god objects—keep per feature.
